headline: High risk of shared-workspace write conflicts and medium risk of prompt/data leakage between two broad-privilege coding agents.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenHands can read/write runtime files and use MCP; Roo Code reads/writes VS Code workspace files and also uses MCP. Because Roo shares state via filesystem and OpenHands shares via mounted volume, attacker-controlled content in shared files or MCP outputs can be treated as instructions by either agent. This is a plausible default pathway, not just manual copy-paste.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mounted workspace or MCP server
IF either agent parses file or MCP content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces or mounts
Disable shared MCP servers for one agent
Add a provenance banner to all inter-agent files
Require manual review before either agent follows instructions from shared files
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging and parser hardening

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch files in shared workspaces and send content to configured model APIs. OpenHands explicitly handles model provider API keys and runtime files; Roo Code touches source code and browser screenshots. If they operate on the same workspace, sensitive file contents can flow into both backends and be exposed through outputs or logs.
conditions: IF the two agents share any workspace directory or mounted volume
IF either agent is configured to upload file contents to its model backend
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for sensitive and non-sensitive tasks
Remove secrets from shared files before running either agent
Turn off browser screenshot capture when not needed
Restrict model API access to least-privilege keys
requires-engineering: add workspace-level data loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, modify git state, and broad network egress. OpenHands shares state via mounted volume, while Roo Code shares state via filesystem and runs with no self-isolation by default. Concurrent edits to the same repo or git branch can overwrite each other or corrupt history, and the blast radius includes irreversible repository state loss.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or workspace path
IF both are allowed to commit, rebase, or rewrite files concurrently
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch
Pause one agent while the other writes
Use file locks around shared directories
Require explicit approval before git mutations
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can act through shell, browser, and MCP, and Roo Code also has shell, browser, and MCP access. If Roo consumes OpenHands output as authoritative, a mistaken plan or fabricated fact can cascade into code changes or browser actions. The reverse pathway exists too, but both profiles show approval gates and agent loops, so this is not the highest severity.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses OpenHands output without verification
IF OpenHands uses Roo Code output as a source of facts or steps
mitigations: Require a verification step before acting on peer output
Ask each agent to cite file paths or commands for claims
Limit one agent to drafting and the other to execution
Review diffs before any commit or browser action
requires-engineering: add structured handoff validation

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source coding agents with docs-only evidence and no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch stated. The main compliance concern is shared handling of model API keys and workspace data, but the profiles do not prove a specific regulatory conflict. I therefore keep this low and do not cite a second-agent compliance gap that is not documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent's workspace
IF the configured model provider or MCP server has retention terms that differ from the operator's policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Review provider retention settings before use
Disable unnecessary logging
Use separate API keys per agent
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
